properties.decision:
Recorded as brainstorming on 2026-09-19 from flo2 F20, not as a proposal, and filed by its reporter as a quality observation rather than a blocker.

THE OBSERVATION: two gap sources answer with a paragraph that routes to who can answer and says whether the thing is even a defect; a third answers with one line. The third is the one that fires once per capability on a design with nothing built — 17 times on flo2's own graph — and a person reads seventeen of those as seventeen defects.

OPTIONS. (a) One sentence in that body saying planned work is a normal state for a young design. Smallest, and it is what the reporter suggests. (b) Have the per-capability finding INHERIT the neighbouring aggregate one, which already states the phase correctly ('Design laid out, but nothing built yet') — structural, and it fixes the class rather than the instance. (c) Suppress the per-capability form entirely while the aggregate holds, so a young design gets one finding instead of seventeen. COUNTER to (c): the aggregate cannot say WHICH capability, and naming them is the useful part once building starts.

⚠️ POSSIBLY DELIBERATE, and the reporter says so. The one-line form may be a considered choice about a detector whose answer really is just a question. What is not deliberate is the asymmetry: the routing and the is-this-a-defect framing were written per detector as each was added, so nothing made the third inherit what the first two carry.
properties.name: OPEN — should a gap body say when the state it reports is a NORMAL phase rather than a defect, given one source fires once per capability on every young design?
